findings.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Applying a default limit of 50 truncates the public membership page, which has no pagination controls, making members beyond the first 50 inaccessible through that page.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates an extra empty page whenever the member count is divisible by the limit; use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:33 — Membership responses unconditionally overwrite offset and members, allowing out-of-order responses from rapid Next/Previous clicks to replace the latest selected page with stale results; ignore stale responses or serialize navigation requests.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify issues related to asynchronous handling of findMembers(). The golden comment points out that findMembers() is now async and unhandled, creating a race condition where member data may not be immediately available. The candidate comment identifies a specific manifestation of this - that out-of-order responses from rapid navigation can overwrite data with stale results. While the candidate is more specific about the race condition scenario (rapid clicks causing stale data), both are fundamentally about the same underlying issue: improper handling of the asynchronous findMembers() call leading to race conditions with member data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Applying a default limit of 50 truncates the public membership page, which has no pagination controls, making members beyond the first 50 inaccessible through that page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the members endpoint in groups_controller.rb now applies a default limit of 50 (line 22). Looking at the public group members template (group/members.hbs), it iterates over 'members' but there are no pagination controls added for the public page - only the admin page (admin/templates/group.hbs) has pagination with next/previous actions. The public route (group-members.js.es6) calls model.findMembers() but doesn't set up pagination controls. This means users beyond the first 50 cannot be accessed on the public group members page.
